title: The router's ledger scan reads and splits a ledger file once for each entry it holds, so a gap-cued question costs about 50 ms
goal: A question the gap or conflict expert scans reads each ledger file once, not once for each entry: kbfacts._ledger_items calls files.setdefault(file, (read(file) or '').splitlines()), whose default is evaluated for every entry, so routed() on a 'What does the kb say about X' question makes 170 reads of _gaps.md; after the fix the repro's count of reads is below 10 and rag.py eval keeps passing all its rows.

run: import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import kbfacts;kbfacts.routed('What does the kb say about Kerberos delegation constrained?');n=[0];r=kbfacts.read;kbfacts.read=lambda p:(n.__setitem__(0,n[0]+1),r(p))[1];kbfacts.routed('What does the kb say about Kerberos delegation constrained?');sys.exit(0 if n[0]<10 else 1)

clauses.clause: A question the gap or conflict expert scans reads each ledger file once, not once for each entry: kbfacts._ledger_items calls files.setdefault(file, (read(file) or '').splitlines()), whose default is evaluated for every entry, so routed() on a 'What does the kb say about X' question makes 170 reads of _gaps.md
after the fix the repro's count of reads is below 10 and rag.py eval keeps passing all its rows

notes: Planned at the 2026-10-13 draft triage (sprint 2 of 15, "Pack notes, router cost and query-log apply guards read what they should"): it serves the fitness tests of EP-gzr4mmkm: a lookup's verdict or the benchmark's measurement is wrong until it is fixed. The rag.py eval check passes before the work: it pins that the fix keeps every eval row passing. Follows BG-apytw7fo (kbfacts.py, test_live_kb.py: the probe's Text class works around the repeated split and can go).
